 Appearance:
Shri Manish Jain - Advocate for the appellants.

Shri Sudarshan Pandit - Advocate for the respondent N
 Order

This misc. appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is preferred for enhancement of Rs.4,00,000/- compensation challenging the award dated 06.03.2025 passed in MACC No.196/2022 by First Member M.A.C.T., Sardarpur, District Dhar (M.P.).
2.
The liability is not disputed.
The quantum is under challenge hence, necessary details are being mentioned.
Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.11,53,656/- regarding death of Mukesh Parmar born on 28.09.1981 (as per Ex.P/15) who died on 17.02.2022 in a motor vehicular accident.

3. Tribunal calculated the loss of dependency taking the age of deceased as 41 years and applied the multiplier of 14 and adding 25% for future prospect and assessing the income as Rs.7,325/- per month on the basis of Rs.293/- per day for 25 days.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:7005 2 MA-4779-2024 4.

This appeal has been preferred on the ground that income has been assessed on the lower side and future prospect has been added 25% instead of 40% and multiplier has been wrongly applied 14 instead of 15.
5.
Learned counsel for the respondent have supported the award.
Perused the record.
6. The age of the deceased was 40 years 04 months and 28 days.
Accordingly, multiplier of 15 is applicable.

Tribunal has treated the deceased as driver hence, per month income of Rs.8,800/-
ought to have been assessed.

Now, the question of future prospect is being considered in light of para 61(iv) of National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Pranay Sethi AIR 2017 SUPREME COURT 5157 which is being reproduced as below:-
"61.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the aforesaid analysis, we proceed to record our conclusions:-
(iv) In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
8. The 40% enhancement is permissible when the age is below years.
In this case, the age of deceased Mukesh is not below the age of 40 years hence, the addition of 25% is permissible.

Accordingly, on re-calculation compensation come as below:-
Future loss of income : Rs.14,85,000/- (Rs.8,800 x 12 + 25% = 1,32,000 x 3/4 =
99,000 x 15) NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:7005 3 MA-4779-2024

Funeral Expenses : Rs.18,000/-
 Loss of Estate : Rs.18,000/-
 Loss of consortium : Rs.1,92,000/- (Appella  (Fillial consortium)
 Total amount : Rs.17,13,000/-
9.
The appeal is partly allowed and Rs. 3,31,344/- (17,13,000- 13,81,656) compensation is further enhanced.
The enhanced amount shall be disbursed as per the award passed by the Tribunal.
With the aforesaid, this misc. appeal is disposed of.
